short_description: Short Form is a publication that offers a fresh perspective on filmmaking. Focusing on some of the most memorable short-...
long_description:
Short Form is a publication that offers a fresh perspective on filmmaking. Focusing on some of the most memorable short-form works in music videos and advertising, the book examines the relevance and evolution of these genres through the forty-year history of Academy Films, one of the UK’s most iconic and influential production companies.


Featuring behind-the-scenes imagery, storyboards, film stills, production notes and other materials, it explores cult pieces that have shaped the cultural and cinematic landscape, such as Jamiroquai’s Virtual Insanity, Lauryn Hill’s Doo Wop (That Thing), Radiohead’s Karma Police, The Verve’s Bittersweet Symphony and FKA Twigs’ M3LL155X, alongside commercials for Guinness, Channel 4 and Levi’s.


With a foreword by filmmaker Jonathan Glazer, the book brings together essays by leading figures in visual culture exploring the history of these projects and their influence on today’s digital short-film landscape.

short_description: How Directors Dress, published by A24 and edited by journalist Charlie Robin Jones, explores the relationship between fa...
long_description:
How Directors Dress, published by A24 and edited by journalist Charlie Robin Jones, explores the relationship between fashion and film through the attire of some of the most prominent directors. The book analyses how the clothing worn during filming can reflect each filmmaker's personality, working style and authority.

Featuring a foreword by British director and screenwriter Joanna Hogg, it brings together photographs, essays and trivia on figures such as Federico Fellini and Wong Kar-Wai. An original look at the semiotics of fashion behind the camera and the way filmmakers construct their own visual identity.

short_description: This posthumous book collects the most intimate memoirs of Eleanor Coppola who, after being diagnosed with a rare cancer...
long_description:
This posthumous book collects the most intimate memoirs of Eleanor Coppola who, after being diagnosed with a rare cancer, reflects on her role as the matriarch of a renowned family of filmmakers and on the creative challenges she faced as an artist during the final years of her life.

The author honestly recounts her effort to balance her role as a wife and mother with her career as a writer and filmmaker, marked by works such as Notes: On the Making of Apocalypse Now and the documentary Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse. An emotional story about family, creation, and resilience in the face of artistic and personal difficulties.

Includes an introduction by Sofia Coppola and an afterword by Alice Waters.

exact_product_name: MM LETTERS BY MM PARIS BOOK (ENGLISH)
short_description: Letters from M/M (Paris) is a comprehensive study of the typefaces created by Michaël Amzalag and Mathias Augustyniak si...
long_description:
Letters from M/M (Paris) is a comprehensive study of the typefaces created by Michaël Amzalag and Mathias Augustyniak since the founding of their influential art and design studio M/M (Paris). The publication brings together for the first time ninety typefaces, chronologically organised into three sections dedicated to their evolution, exclusive typographic specimens, and detailed illustrations of the projects in which they have been used.

Written and designed by typography expert Paul McNeil, with a foreword by Björk, the book explores the importance of letters, symbols, and signs in the work of M/M (Paris), ranging from artistic commissions and identity projects for fashion houses to collaborations with musicians and theatres.

A reference work aimed at graphic designers, historians, students, and lovers of art, design, and visual culture.

short_description: This edition explores the concept of true icons, inspired by the Oxford Dictionary definition: people or things admired ...
long_description:
This edition explores the concept of true icons, inspired by the Oxford Dictionary definition: people or things admired that represent an idea or a way of life. On this occasion, the spotlight is on Lauren Hutton, one of the most influential models in history, whose authenticity, free spirit, and unique vision have redefined the fashion industry for nearly six decades.

Through a journey across her extraordinary career, the publication revisits her close collaboration with photographer Richard Avedon, the signing of the first million-dollar contract for a model, and her passion for traveling the world, driven by the desire to discover new cultures beyond the runway. Her memories of figures like Diana Vreeland and her travels through Morocco, Persia, or Bali reflect a life marked by curiosity, independence, and adventure.

Furthermore, this edition brings together a curated selection of interviews, features, and collaborations with prominent names in art, fashion, design, and architecture—including Boucheron, Dries Van Noten, Joseph Dirand, François Halard, The Row, Saint Laurent, Hauser & Wirth, Jacques Garcia, and Urban Jürgensen—offering a sophisticated look at the contemporary creative universe.

short_description: This magazine presents an editorial vision where fashion, art and contemporary culture engage in a free and experimental...
long_description:
This magazine presents an editorial vision where fashion, art and contemporary culture engage in a free and experimental dialogue. The cover features Nikki Lilly, photographed by Jordan Hemingway and dressed in a creation by Matières Fécales, setting a provocative, conceptual and deeply creative tone from the start.

The Spring-Summer 2026 issue brings together fashion editorials from some of the most innovative brands and creators of the moment, including Paolo Carzana, Comme des Garçons and Matières Fécales, with imagery by acclaimed photographers such as Paolo Roversi, Jordan Hemingway, Laura Marie Cieplik and Tim Gutt. The publication pairs these productions with conversations and profiles dedicated to artists, writers and cultural figures such as Doris Lessing, Prunella Clough, Isabella Ducrot, Paul Thek and Beuford Smith, offering a broad perspective on art, literature and contemporary creation.

Beyond fashion, the magazine explores themes related to community, identity, gastronomy, photography and performance through essays, interviews and features such as Joy is Resistance, Capturing Community, Cooking for Ninety People and Studio as Art. Marc Springhetti’s paintings, featured throughout the edition, reinforce the artistic character of the publication and create a visual thread connecting its various sections.

With a creative direction committed to experimentation and interdisciplinary collaboration, this edition becomes an editorial object where fashion transcends clothing to converse with art, music, design and contemporary thought, solidifying its status as a reference magazine for those seeking an avant-garde vision of current culture.
